author: bigdog3700
quote: I have finished the game and plenty of side activities and I came away from GTA 6 pretty disappointed. I absolutely loved the graphics, the level of detail in the world, and the gameplay itself. The combat, shooting, and overall mechanics were enjoyable, the game is just visually impressive. However, I was really disappointed by the 30 FPS cap on the PS5 Pro, which made the experience feel less smooth than I would have liked. My bigger issues were with the writing, voice acting, and overall characterization. A lot of the dialogue felt awkward, unnatural, or strangely delivered, and many conversations lacked genuine emotion or personality. Some characters felt flat, dull, or difficult to connect with, and certain scenes that should have carried some emotional weight (as much as GTA game possibly can) just didn't land for me. Jason felt unusually lifeless, with a monotone delivery that made it difficult to get invested in his character. The writing also felt inconsistent, sometimes trying to be serious or emotional but failing to make those moments feel believable or impactful. I was also disappointed with how restricted the overall freedom of choice felt. For a game of this scale, I expected more player agency, more ways to approach situations, and more freedom to make decisions that genuinely affect how things play out. At times, it felt like I was being pushed through a predetermined experience rather than given the freedom that I associate with GTA. On top of that, I felt like the game was missing a lot of the humor and entertaining, memorable moments that make GTA so enjoyable in the first place. There weren't nearly as many genuinely funny cutscenes, ridiculous situations, memorable interactions, or moments of pure chaos as I expected. A lot of the game felt oddly serious, subdued, or just lacking personality, and I rarely found myself laughing or experiencing those unexpected moments that make GTA memorable.
